newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- unchanged, looking at supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- unchanged, looking at supply.

text.p: The U.S. municipal market in early trade on Tuesday was broadly unchanged, as traders pondered whether a recent drop in yields would continue to pull refundings into the new issuance arena.
"We're unchanged to down an 1/8. If the market keeps going lower, hopefully, some of these refundings won't come in," a trader said.
Yet another trader said that while some bonds were quoted a bit lower, others were seen up 0.01 basis point.
Among early pricings, $95 million of Washington Health Care Facilities were priced at a top yield of 5.40 percent in 2017.
A nearly $25 million balance remained on a $36.55 million sale by The School District of Pittsburgh, Allegheney County, Pennslyvania, which on Monday sold the general obligations.
The main gauge of the secondary market, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, edged down to just over $1.3 billion from to $1.38 billion on Monday.
Insitutional players appeared to be seeking higher-coupon bonds, which would offer more protection if prices kept edging lower, and shedding more vulnerable, lower-yielding paper.
"I don't know if they're not as bullish or if they just keep fighting it," a trader said, referring to the market's recent rise, though prices have softened slightly.
"It's very hard to continue to be bullish when you're at the top of something," he added later, pegging the range on Treasury futures at from 114-28/32 to 115-24/32.
In Chicago, September Treasury bond futures were unchanged at 115-14/32, while September municipal bond futures rose one tick to 121-2/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 180 ticks.

The main data due Tuesday, the second quarter Employment Cost Index, prompted an early dip in the Treasury market, but prices later recovered. The report showed an overall 0.8 percent rise, which was in line with the increase forecast by economists.
Wages and salaries, which account for about 70 percent of the overall index, also jumped 0.8 percent in the second quarter, after rising 0.9 percent in the first quarter.
Benefit costs rose 0.6 percent, compared with a 0.1 percent rise in the previous three-month period.

Actively quoted bonds in the secondary market included Harris County, Texas, Refunding, Toll Road bonds of 2024, which pay a five percent coupon, and were bid at 5.31 percent, NET, down two basis points.
And Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.48 percent, NET, down one basis point.
